skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos through the inference.sh Belt CLI. Supports dimensions, FPS, duration, codec, props, and common Remotion APIs.
skill.summary: Convert Remotion component code into configurable MP4 renders through inference.sh.
skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: Most static Ruby backtick findings are Markdown formatting, code fences, or documentation examples and were dismissed. Confirmed issues are the intended Belt CLI execution path, external installation commands, and reliance on inference.sh for remote rendering. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The Belt CLI allowlist is broad.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the exact Belt render subcommands and arguments needed by this skill.

remediation.issue: Render requests upload TSX code and props to inference.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy warning and tell users not to include secrets, tokens, or private customer data.

remediation.issue: The skill includes external installation commands and setup links.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer versioned, signed, or pinned installation instructions for the required CLI and related skills.

static_findings.snippet: > **Install the belt CLI skill:** `npx skills add belt-sh/cli`
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

content.value_statement: Programmatic video rendering is difficult when teams need repeatable motion graphics from React components. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to call the inference.sh renderer with Remotion inputs.
actual_capabilities: Runs the Belt CLI command for the infsh/remotion-render app.
Accepts Remotion TSX code that exports a default component.
Supports props, composition IDs, duration, FPS, width, height, and codec settings.
Documents common Remotion imports such as AbsoluteFill, Sequence, spring, and interpolate.
Shows CLI and Python SDK workflows for rendering and progress streaming.
Returns rendered video output from the inference.sh service.
limitations: Requires a working inference.sh account and authenticated Belt CLI.
Uploads render code and props to a third-party service.
Does not validate the safety of submitted TSX code locally.
Only documents Remotion and React imports listed by the skill.

use_cases.title: Create reusable motion graphics
use_cases.description: Frontend engineers can render React animation components into MP4 assets for product launches and demos.

use_cases.title: Render data-driven explainers
use_cases.description: Data teams can turn chart logic and props into repeatable videos with controlled dimensions and duration.

use_cases.title: Produce social video variants
use_cases.description: Marketing teams can render branded text, counters, and sequences without manual timeline editing.

prompt_templates.title: Render a simple title
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a three second Remotion title video with fade-in text, 1920 by 1080 resolution, and 30 FPS.

prompt_templates.title: Create a branded animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Remotion animation using our brand colors, a spring entrance, and an MP4 output suitable for a product demo.

prompt_templates.title: Render a sequenced explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a sequence-based Remotion video with three timed sections, props for text values, and a square 60 FPS render.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a production render
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a render plan with explicit duration, codec, dimensions, composition ID, props, and progress streaming for review.

output_examples.input: Render a short welcome title with a dark background and white text.
output_examples.output: A three second MP4 with smooth text fade-in, 1920 by 1080 resolution, and 30 FPS playback.

output_examples.input: Create a product metric counter for a square social post.
output_examples.output: A square MP4 showing an animated percentage counter, controlled timing, and simple branded layout.

output_examples.input: Render a multi-step explainer using supplied title and subtitle values.
output_examples.output: A timed Remotion video with sequential sections, passed-in text values, and a returned video link.

best_practices: Review generated TSX before sending it to the remote renderer.
Use explicit width, height, FPS, and duration for predictable renders.
Keep props small and avoid secrets or private customer data.
anti_patterns: Do not submit source code that contains credentials or private tokens.
Do not rely on default render settings for production assets.
Do not ask the agent to install unrelated skills during a render task.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion component code into MP4 video through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it require a separate account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects an authenticated inference.sh Belt CLI session.

faq.question: Can I control video settings?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented inputs include width, height, FPS, duration, codec, props, and composition ID.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is submitted code kept local?
faq.answer: No. The render request sends TSX code and props to the inference.sh service.

faq.question: Does the skill check Remotion code quality?
faq.answer: No. It documents rendering workflows but does not perform local security or quality validation.
